name: Deepaprakasa Perumal Temple, Thoopul
deity: Vishnu as Deepaprakasa — Vilakkoli Perumal, the Lord of the lamp's radiance — with the Goddess Maragathavalli
period: A Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu in Kanchipuram, praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; birthplace of Vedanta Desika
summary: At Thoopul in Kanchipuram, Vishnu shines as Deepaprakasa, the Lord of the lamp's radiance — a Divya Desam of Thondai Nadu and the birthplace of the great acharya Vedanta Desika, whose shrine stands within.

sections.history: Thiruthanka, the Divya Desam at Thoopul in Kanchipuram, is one of the 108 Divya Desams and one of the fourteen in the city, in the heart of Thondai Nadu. Its Lord is Deepaprakasa — in Tamil, Vilakkoli Perumal, the radiance of the lamp — and the shrine is praised in the Nalayira Divya Prabandham; tradition credits its hymn to Thirumangai Alvar. Thoopul holds a further, special honour: it is the birthplace of Vedanta Desika, the poet-philosopher born here in 1268 who became one of the foremost teachers of Sri Vaishnavism, so that he is remembered as Thoopul Vedanta Desikan. A shrine to Desika stands within the temple, and devotees of his lineage come here as to a home.
sections.architecture: A compact temple in the Dravidian manner of Kanchipuram, entered through a gateway tower into a court that gathers three centres of devotion: the sanctum of Deepaprakasa, the shrine of the Goddess Maragathavalli, and the shrine of Vedanta Desika, honoured within the temple of his birthplace. Pillared halls lead to the sanctum, where lamps fittingly frame the Lord whose very name is light.
sections.legends: The Lord's name tells his story: Deepaprakasa, the light of the lamp. Kanchi's sthala tradition, as commonly told, sets the shrine in the cycle of Brahma's great sacrifice — when darkness was sent to engulf the world and halt the rite, Vishnu shone forth as a radiant lamp and the sacrifice went on. For devotees the image also carries a second light: that of Vedanta Desika, born beside this temple, whose teaching lit the path of the tradition.
sections.festivals: The birth-star of Vedanta Desika in the month of Purattasi (September–October) is the season of greatest devotion at his birthplace. The temple also keeps the Vaishnava year of Kanchipuram — Vaikunta Ekadashi in Margazhi and the annual festival of the presiding Lord. Confirm festival dates locally.
sections.experience: Come to light a lamp before Vilakkoli Perumal, the Lord of light, and then stand before Vedanta Desika in the place where he was born. Students and followers of Desika's teaching make this a quiet pilgrimage of gratitude. It fits naturally into a day among Kanchipuram's many Divya Desams.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Purattasi festival days are busiest. Confirm current timings locally before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: It lies within Kanchipuram town, which has a railway station and is reached by road from Chennai (around 70 km); Chennai has the nearest major airport.
